title: Diogenes: History's Wildest Philosopher
hook: Diogenes lived inside a ceramic wine jar and told Alexander the Great to get out of his sunlight.

scenes.text: While Plato and Aristotle taught wealthy aristocrats in private academies, Diogenes of Sinope took philosophy straight into the gutter.

scenes.voicedText: While Plato and Aristotle taught wealthy aristocrats in private academies, Diogenes of Sinope took philosophy straight into the gutter.

scenes.text: He rejected all material possessions, living in a massive ceramic storage jar called a pithos in the Athenian marketplace.

scenes.text: Diogenes famously walked through Athens in broad daylight carrying a lit oil lamp, telling confused citizens he was 'looking for an honest man'.

scenes.text: When Plato defined man as a 'featherless biped', Diogenes plucked a live chicken, brought it into Plato's lecture hall, and shouted: 'Behold! Plato's man!'

scenes.text: When Alexander the Great visited and offered to grant any wish, Diogenes casually squinted and replied: 'Yes, stand out of my sunlight.'
